name: Marcus — strong pilot, no particular plans
summary: Sixty-odd hours over three seasons, out most weeks at his club hill, excellent on the ground, flies moderate thermals, reads the day well, reserve practised and repacked, instructor has already said he'd be fine on a low-B. His A is getting old and he needs a wing anyway. Asked what he wants from the next year, he ticks 'nothing in particular — just enjoying it'.
why_this_persona: The suggestion-floor regression case. He is a strong, well-prepared pilot with no specific weakness to advise on and no exposure-bound ambition, so almost nothing in the suggestions config fires for him. Under v2 that meant exactly two suggestions — instructor_conversation (always) and test_fly_first (fires on a ready result) — against a stated minimum of three. He exists to keep the always pool large enough that the floor is actually reachable from the strongest end of the answer space, not just the weakest.

notes: Added in v3. The exclude list above is deliberately exhaustive — it is every suggestion in config/suggestions/a-to-low-b.json except the four he must trigger. That is the assertion that actually locks the regression: if a future edit makes any gap-specific suggestion fire for a pilot with no gaps, this persona fails, and if either new always suggestion is removed or made conditional, this persona fails too.

He triggers exactly four suggestions, on four distinct topics (instructor, wing_choice, currency, progression), so topic dedupe cannot collapse the displayed set below four. Under v2 he triggered two, which is below meta.selection.min_shown of 3 — the reviewer finding this persona exists to close.

Computed by hand from config/scoring/a-to-low-b.json: skills 127.4/130 = 98.0 (landing_accuracy 0.85, active_piloting 0.9, collapse_experience 0.9, descent_bigears 0.9, everything else 1.0); psychological 65.7/75 = 87.6 (upgrade_motivation 0.65, learning_curve 0.85, response_when_rough 0.85, incidents 0.85, rest 1.0); total 0.55 x 98.0 + 0.45 x 87.6 = 93.3, no bonus.

'replacing_anyway' (0.65) is the realistic motive for a pilot in his position — his wing is worn out — and is the single biggest drag on his psychological score. It must not trigger 'motivation_reframe_keeping_up' or 'motivation_reframe_equipment_fix' and must not fire the 'equipment_as_a_fix_with_thin_readiness' gate, since it is neither a comparison motive nor an expectation that the wing will fix anything.

He meets the 'local_only' intended_flying_context profile through 'just_enjoy' alone, with no 'local_soaring' tick — the branch knowledge/disagreements-driven profile definition allows but no other persona covers. It is inert for him because he answers 'rough_air_awareness: plan_around_it', so neither the stated-plans exemption nor 'scope_matches_your_plans' is in play. 'exemptions_expected' is empty for exactly that reason, and a scorer that reports an exemption for him is applying it without the triggering answer.

Reviewer check: his result must not read as a reward, and the two always suggestions must not read as filler. Both have to be true and useful for a pilot already doing everything right — one is about protecting a habit he already has, the other is about the step after this one.
